what_was_done: When the literal matches no spelling of the resolved root, _anchored anchors it as Path(os.path.realpath(literal.parent)) / literal.name and returns it when that lands under the root: the ancestor symlinks collapse to the root and a symlink at the leaf stays literal. ctx.project.root is resolved (built from ctx.target), so the old spelled != root branch never fired and an ancestor-symlinked spelling got only the resolved form classed. test_spelling_through_symlinked_alias_classes_both_forms spells the brief through a symlinked alias of tmp_path (the portable spelling of the macOS /var case) and asserts ('brief', 'spec-product', 'source', 'project'); deleting the fallback fails it, as does spelling the alias through /var on macOS.

The 'outside' drop is gone from _union: the union keeps every class of both forms, so an in-project symlink whose destination is outside the project, the plugin directory and tmp answers 'project' and 'outside' together, and a read-walls rule (H3) reading ctx.classes sees the destination's outside. The plan 3.1 interfaces keep their names and signatures (ctx.classes, ctx.classes_of, paths.classes_of); no per-form split is exposed — the literal and resolved classes are available separately only inside paths.py — because walls' read_allow shape is a step 4 question; expose it there if it is wanted. test_in_project_symlink_outside_stays_outside links src/wall-peek to /etc/hosts and asserts ('unclassified', 'project', 'outside'); restoring the drop fails it, and it was the only test noticing.
